strings.path.title: Alternate Picking
strings.path.goal: Pick a clean, even line in A minor across all six strings, and hold it over a band for eight bars.
strings.path.assumes: You can fret single notes cleanly, you hold a pick, and you can play eighth notes with a click at 80 BPM. No speed is assumed. The minutes listed are one pass through the material; expect to come back to each Step for days or weeks.
strings.path.gradingLimits: Everything here is graded on timing and notes for single picked notes, which is what the app is built for, and none of it has been tried on a real guitar yet. The faster the line, the less sure the grade. Your setup adds a small delay between playing a note and the app hearing it; up to sixteenths at 100 BPM that makes no difference, and above that, read the evenness score as provisional. Heavy distortion and compression blur where each note starts, so a clean or light-crunch tone is the honest setting for a graded take. Nothing faster than sixteenths at 200 BPM is graded, and no Exercise here goes that far.
strings.path.skills.1: Eighth notes with a click at 80 BPM
strings.step.even-eighths.title: Even eighths on one string
strings.step.even-eighths.goal: Down-up, down-up, every note the same length, at the speed of a slow walk.
strings.step.even-eighths.why: Every later Step is this motion, faster or across strings. If eighths are uneven at 80 BPM, sixteenths at 120 will only hide it for a while. One string means there is only one thing to think about: time.
strings.step.even-eighths.howTo.0: Hold the pick between thumb and the side of the first finger, with a little of its tip showing. Move it from the wrist, small, like shaking water off the end of a finger.
strings.step.even-eighths.howTo.1: Down on the beat, up on the 'and'. The pick stays in the same place above and below the string and travels as little as it can.
strings.step.even-eighths.howTo.2: Rest the side of the picking hand lightly on the bridge so the low strings stay quiet.
strings.step.even-eighths.payoff: A tune over an open string that sits on the click from the first Exercise, and a riff that already sounds like a riff.
strings.exercise.even-eighths.open-string.title: A tune over the open E
strings.exercise.even-eighths.open-string.purpos: A melody in A minor with the open high E sounding between every note, the pedal-tone sound of a baroque prelude or a rock guitar's showpiece, slowed right down. The fretting hand moves once a beat, so nearly all your attention stays on the pick.
Eighth notes on the high E string, 60 BPM up to a pass at 100. Downstroke on every fretted note, upstroke on every open E: strictly down-up, never two the same way.

The tune is C, B, A, B, then C, D, C, B, then C, B, A, G#, then A, G#, A, B, and round again. First finger on fret 5, third on 7, fourth on 8. Move the hand up two frets for the D at fret 10 in bar 2, and back one fret in bars 3 and 4, so the first finger takes the G# at 4 and the second the A at 5.
Each open E is your time to move the fretting hand. Keep down and up equally loud: uneven pick depth is the usual reason they are not.
strings.exercise.even-eighths.open-string.coachL: Even eighths and the written notes are what I check, after the take. The direction of each stroke is yours to keep: I can't hear it.
strings.exercise.even-eighths.four-fingers.title: Four fingers, one string
strings.exercise.even-eighths.four-fingers.purpo: Bring the fretting hand in without letting it set the time. The fingers land exactly when the pick does.
strings.exercise.even-eighths.four-fingers.howTo: First finger on fret 5, one finger per fret. Walk up and back on the A string.
Keep each finger down until the next one lands, and keep the little finger close to the string.
strings.exercise.even-eighths.four-fingers.coach: If the notes bunch up, slow down one rung. Timing is what I have to go on here.
strings.exercise.even-eighths.a-minor-one-string: Your first melody, played by moving the whole hand along the G string, so shifts stop being an event.
Play the A natural minor scale along the G string with the first two fingers only, sliding the hand between notes. Lift just enough to move.
Sing the notes if you can. A wrong note here is obvious to the ear.
After the take I can say whether the notes were the written ones, and how even they were.
strings.exercise.even-eighths.pedal-riff.title: The low E riff
strings.exercise.even-eighths.pedal-riff.purpose: The audible payoff: a palm-muted riff in E. Alternate strokes on a low string feel different, and this is where it counts.
strings.exercise.even-eighths.pedal-riff.howTo.0: Rest the side of your palm on the low E, just in front of the bridge, so the open string thuds and still has a pitch.
strings.exercise.even-eighths.pedal-riff.howTo.1: Strictly down-up, even on the repeated open notes. Rock players often use all downstrokes here; this Exercise is deliberately not that.
strings.exercise.even-eighths.pedal-riff.coachLi: I can time the riff and check its notes after the take. Whether the palm mute sounds right is your ear's job.
strings.step.even-sixteenths.title: Even sixteenths on one string
strings.step.even-sixteenths.goal: The same motion at twice the rate, without the hand tightening to get there.
strings.step.even-sixteenths.why: Sixteenths are where picking stops being counting and starts being a motion you trust. Doubling the rate exposes any stroke that was bigger than it needed to be, and it is the first place a click and a hand really disagree.
strings.step.even-sixteenths.howTo.0: Make the stroke smaller, not harder. If you feel your forearm lock, slow down one rung: the locked arm is usually what makes the wall.
strings.step.even-sixteenths.howTo.1: Count '1 e and a'. Down on 1 and 'and', up on 'e' and 'a'.
strings.step.even-sixteenths.howTo.2: Tilt the pick slightly so its edge slides off the string rather than digging in.
strings.step.even-sixteenths.payoff: A run of sixteenths you can hold for a full loop, and a melody that sounds busy without feeling frantic.
strings.exercise.even-sixteenths.gear-change.pur: The open-E tune from the first Step, then the same notes twice as fast. Going from eighths to sixteenths without a stumble is the real skill, because every line changes rate.
strings.exercise.even-sixteenths.gear-change.how: Bar 1 is eighths: C, B, A, B with the open E between each. Bar 2 is sixteenths: the first two bars of the open-E tune, C, B, A, B, C, D, C, B, squeezed into one. 50 BPM up to a pass at 85.
Down on every fretted note, up on every open E, in both bars. The stroke gets smaller in bar 2, not harder; the pick never skips.
strings.exercise.even-sixteenths.gear-change.coa: I'll say how even each half was, and check the notes after the take. The join between the bars is usually where it slips.
strings.exercise.even-sixteenths.gear-change.det: At this speed a real rig's input delay can push notes out of their matching window, which reads as late or missed. Evenness is the number to trust here, and only once the delay is calibrated.
strings.exercise.even-sixteenths.four-fingers-16: The hands have to agree at a rate where they can no longer be managed one note at a time.
The same walk as before, at sixteenths. If the fingers run ahead of the pick, the notes come out as flams; make the fingers lazier.
Evenness is the number to watch on this one.
At this speed a real rig's input delay can push notes out of their matching window, which reads as late or missed. Evenness is the number to trust here, and only once the delay is calibrated.
A melody where the fretting hand moves once a beat and the pick never stops: the rate in the right hand, the music in the left.
Four sixteenths per note on the top string. Move the left hand exactly on the beat, not a hair before.
This is the tremolo idea in slow motion, and it is a good warm-up on any day.
Four notes per pitch makes the time easy to judge, and I'll check the notes after the take.
At this speed a real rig's input delay can push notes out of their matching window, which reads as late or missed. Evenness is the number to trust here, and only once the delay is calibrated.
strings.exercise.even-sixteenths.b-string-melody: Sixteenth melody on the B string
A real line in A minor on one string: if this one sings, your sixteenths are musical rather than merely fast.
Stay on the B string and shift by small moves. Let the first note of each beat be a touch stronger so you can hear where you are.
When this is even and on the written notes, the next Step is ready for you.
At this speed a real rig's input delay can push notes out of their matching window, which reads as late or missed. Evenness is the number to trust here, and only once the delay is calibrated.
strings.step.accents.title: Accents where you want them
strings.step.accents.goal: Put a louder note on any sixteenth you choose, including the ones on an upstroke, without the time moving.
strings.step.accents.why: Accents prove the picking hand is under control rather than running on its own, and they are what makes a fast line sound like rhythm. An accent on an upstroke is the honest test: most players can only accent downstrokes until they practise this.
strings.step.accents.howTo.0: An accent comes from a little more depth and speed in that one stroke. Don't squeeze, and don't let the next note get swallowed.
strings.step.accents.howTo.1: Keep the unaccented notes quiet on purpose. The contrast is what makes an accent, more than the loud note does.
strings.step.accents.howTo.2: Use a clean or light-crunch tone. Compression and high gain flatten the difference, for your ear and for the app.
strings.step.accents.payoff: The same run of notes that used to sound like a typewriter now has a groove in it.
strings.exercise.accents.on-the-beat.title: Accent every beat
strings.exercise.accents.on-the-beat.purpose: The easy case first: the accent falls on a downstroke, and every beat is marked.
strings.exercise.accents.on-the-beat.howTo.0: Accent the first note of each group of four. If everything gets louder, your unaccented notes have crept up.
strings.exercise.accents.on-the-beat.coachLine: Accent checks are rough: I can only tell louder from not louder.
strings.exercise.accents.on-the-beat.detection.0: At this speed a real rig's input delay can push notes out of their matching window, which reads as late or missed. Evenness is the number to trust here, and only once the delay is calibrated.
strings.exercise.accents.on-the-beat.detection.1: Accents are measured roughly, as louder than the notes either side. Compression and high gain flatten them.
strings.exercise.accents.walking-accent.title: Walk the accent
strings.exercise.accents.walking-accent.purpose: One note, four bars, and the accent moves from the first sixteenth to the last. Bars 2 and 4 are accents on upstrokes.
strings.exercise.accents.walking-accent.howTo.0: Same note throughout. Change which note of the four is loud at each bar line, and keep the time dead still while you do.
strings.exercise.accents.walking-accent.coachLin: Bars 2 and 4 are the test. The accent readout is rough, so trust your ear too.
strings.exercise.accents.walking-accent.detectio: Accents are measured roughly, as louder than the notes either side. Compression and high gain flatten them.
strings.exercise.accents.three-over-four.title: Threes across fours
strings.exercise.accents.three-over-four.purpose: Accents every three sixteenths turn a straight line into a pattern that pulls against the beat: this is the payoff of the Step.
strings.exercise.accents.three-over-four.howTo.0: Accents fall at 3, 3, 3, 3, 4 sixteenths. Tap your foot on the beat, not on the accents, and let the two disagree.
strings.exercise.accents.three-over-four.coachLi: Your accents should fall against the click here, which makes this a good one to listen back to.
strings.exercise.accents.three-over-four.detecti: At this speed a real rig's input delay can push notes out of their matching window, which reads as late or missed. Evenness is the number to trust here, and only once the delay is calibrated.
Accents are measured roughly, as louder than the notes either side. Compression and high gain flatten them.
strings.exercise.accents.melody-on-accents.title: A melody on the accents
strings.exercise.accents.melody-on-accents.purpo: Fretted accents over an open-string pedal: the tune is only in the loud notes, and you are the one making it come out.
strings.exercise.accents.melody-on-accents.howTo: Between accents the open E keeps going, quietly. Move the fretting hand during the open notes so the accented note is there in time.
strings.exercise.accents.melody-on-accents.coach: If the melody jumps out when you listen back, the Exercise has done its job. I can only check that the accents were louder.
strings.exercise.accents.melody-on-accents.detec: At this speed a real rig's input delay can push notes out of their matching window, which reads as late or missed. Evenness is the number to trust here, and only once the delay is calibrated.
Accents are measured roughly, as louder than the notes either side. Compression and high gain flatten them.
strings.step.crossing.title: Crossing two strings
strings.step.crossing.goal: Change strings with no gap and no scrape, on both kinds of crossing.
strings.step.crossing.why: This is where alternate picking actually gets hard. On one string the pick has nothing in its way; between two strings it has to get over one of them. There are only two kinds of crossing, and every line in the rest of this Path is built from them.
strings.step.crossing.howTo.0: Outside: a downstroke on the lower-pitched string, then an upstroke on the higher one. Each stroke starts from outside the pair, so the pick travels around the strings.
strings.step.crossing.howTo.1: Inside: an upstroke on the lower-pitched string, then a downstroke on the higher one. Each stroke starts between the two strings, so the pick must hop out of the gap.
strings.step.crossing.howTo.2: Let the pick clear the strings by as little as you can. Much of this motion comes from a small tilt of the wrist, so try it slowly with no click first.
strings.step.crossing.payoff: A short A minor lick that used to trip every time now rolls, and you can name which crossing is the one that catches you.
strings.exercise.crossing.outside-shuttle.title: Outside, two notes
strings.exercise.crossing.outside-shuttle.purpos: One outside crossing, over and over, with nothing else to think about.
Down on the G string, up on the B string, slowly. Your pick travels around the outside of the pair.
strings.exercise.crossing.outside-shuttle.coachL: I can time these and hear if notes go missing. Which way the pick went is up to you to keep honest.
strings.exercise.crossing.inside-shuttle.title: Inside, two notes
strings.exercise.crossing.inside-shuttle.purpose: The same two notes, starting from the top string so that the pick is trapped between them. Most players feel the difference at once.
strings.exercise.crossing.inside-shuttle.howTo.0: Down on the B string, up on the G string. The pick works inside the gap and has to escape at each change.
strings.exercise.crossing.inside-shuttle.coachLi: If this one is uneven and the last one was not, that is useful to know. Stay at the tempo that stays even.
strings.exercise.crossing.outside-moving.title: Outside, moving notes
strings.exercise.crossing.outside-moving.purpose: A moving pair at sixteenths, all outside crossings, so the fretting hand gets busier while the pick path stays the same.
strings.exercise.crossing.outside-moving.howTo.0: Sixteenths on the G and B strings, each pair twice: C and E, D and G, C and F, D and E. First finger on the frets at 5, third finger on the G string's 7, second on the B string's 6, little finger on its 8.
strings.exercise.crossing.outside-moving.howTo.1: The strokes never change: down on the G string, up on the B string. Only the fretting hand has anything new to do.
strings.exercise.crossing.outside-moving.coachLi: Evenness plus the right notes, after the take.
strings.exercise.crossing.outside-moving.detecti: At this speed a real rig's input delay can push notes out of their matching window, which reads as late or missed. Evenness is the number to trust here, and only once the delay is calibrated.
strings.exercise.crossing.inside-moving.title: Inside, moving notes
strings.exercise.crossing.inside-moving.purpose: The same four pairs, top note first, all inside crossings, so you can compare the two honestly.
strings.exercise.crossing.inside-moving.howTo.0: The same four pairs in sixteenths with the B string first: E and C, G and D, F and C, E and D, each twice.
strings.exercise.crossing.inside-moving.howTo.1: Down on the B string, up on the G string. If you hear a tiny gap at each change, that is the pick hopping out from between the strings. Make the hop smaller, not faster.
strings.exercise.crossing.inside-moving.coachLin: Compare this take with the outside one. The gap between them is what you are working on.
strings.exercise.crossing.inside-moving.detectio: At this speed a real rig's input delay can push notes out of their matching window, which reads as late or missed. Evenness is the number to trust here, and only once the delay is calibrated.
strings.exercise.crossing.outside-lick.title: An all-outside A minor lick
strings.exercise.crossing.outside-lick.purpose: Eight notes that sound like a real lick and happen to contain only outside crossings. This is the Step's payoff.
strings.exercise.crossing.outside-lick.howTo.0: Start on a downstroke on the D string. Every string change works out as outside; keep that going by never adding a stroke.
strings.exercise.crossing.outside-lick.coachLine: This is music now. Get it even, then speed it up one rung at a time.
strings.exercise.crossing.outside-lick.detection: At this speed a real rig's input delay can push notes out of their matching window, which reads as late or missed. Evenness is the number to trust here, and only once the delay is calibrated.
strings.step.pentatonic-patterns.title: Pentatonic patterns
strings.step.pentatonic-patterns.goal: Play the A minor pentatonic box in the sequences you actually hear in rock and blues solos.
strings.step.pentatonic-patterns.why: Two notes per string means a crossing every other note, and the same kind of crossing each time. That is exactly what makes pentatonic runs harder to pick than they look, and it is why they come right after crossings. You get a sound you already recognise as your reward.
strings.step.pentatonic-patterns.howTo.0: Starting on a downstroke on the first note of a string, every change going up is inside. Coming down from a downstroke on the first note of a string, every change is outside. Where the stroke falls decides it, so you can choose.
strings.step.pentatonic-patterns.howTo.1: Roll a fingertip across when two notes share a fret on neighbouring strings, rather than lifting and placing it.
strings.step.pentatonic-patterns.howTo.2: Use a click on the quarter note and let the triplets feel round.
strings.step.pentatonic-patterns.payoff: The run from a hundred solos you have heard, at a tempo where it is clean, and the same lick working in three keys.
strings.exercise.pentatonic-patterns.box-up-down: The whole box in plain triplets, so the map and the crossings settle together.

Six strings up and back. The turn on the top string lands the next downstroke on the box's lower fret, so the descent is inside crossings too: the whole loop is one kind, and you get a long look at it.
I'll say whether the notes were the box and how even they were.
strings.exercise.pentatonic-patterns.inside-shut: Inside on two strings of the box
Six notes, all inside crossings, isolated from the hardest corner of the pentatonic.
G and B strings. Start down on the G string. Both crossings are inside, and there is no easy one to rest on.
This is the corner the long runs trip on. Evenness tells the story.
strings.exercise.pentatonic-patterns.threes-down: The classic pentatonic run: groups of three coming down the box, each group starting one note lower.
Triplets, so every group starts on a beat. Three is odd, so each group starts on the opposite stroke from the last one, which is the whole point: the crossings keep changing.
A long run like this usually slips in the same place. Listening back will show you where.
strings.exercise.pentatonic-patterns.fours-up.pu: Sixteenths in groups of four climbing the box: harder than threes, because more of the crossings fall on the weak part of the beat.
strings.exercise.pentatonic-patterns.fours-up.ho: Say the group's first note to yourself. It lands on every beat, so if you lose it you have lost the sequence.
strings.exercise.pentatonic-patterns.fours-up.co: Stay on a rung that keeps it even. Fast and rough teaches the wrong thing here.
strings.exercise.pentatonic-patterns.lick-in-thr: Your all-outside lick moved through A, D and E minor pentatonic, so the shape stops being tied to fret 5.
Two bars at fret 5, one at fret 10, one at fret 12. Shift during the last note of the bar. The strokes do not change.
The shift is the risk. If a note goes missing, look at the bar line first.
strings.step.three-per-string.title: Three notes per string
strings.step.three-per-string.goal: Run the A minor scale in three-per-string shapes, where the crossing type changes on every string.
strings.step.three-per-string.why: An odd number of notes per string flips the stroke at each change, so outside and inside crossings take turns. This is the shape of most fast scalar playing, and it gives you a long scale without a position shift to manage.
strings.step.three-per-string.howTo.0: Each string has three notes, fretted with first, second and little fingers or first, third and little fingers, depending on the gaps. Open the hand from the first finger; don't twist the wrist to reach.
strings.step.three-per-string.howTo.1: Keep the thumb relaxed behind the neck. It should not be squeezing against your fingers.
strings.step.three-per-string.howTo.2: Ascending, the changes alternate outside then inside. Say which one is next until you stop needing to.
strings.step.three-per-string.payoff: A two-octave A minor run, and a six-note lick you will use for the rest of your life.
A classic six-note cell on the top two strings in which both crossings are inside. It is a real lick, not a drill.
C, B, A on the top string, then G, F, E on the B string, all in triplets. Start on a downstroke, and it stays down on each repeat.
Even triplets first. This one is worth owning at a slow tempo before it gets fast.
strings.exercise.three-per-string.six-note-up.pu: The mirror image, in which both crossings are outside, so the two versions tell you which hop you own.
strings.exercise.three-per-string.six-note-up.ho: Triplets: E, F, G on the B string (frets 5, 6, 8), then A, B, C on the top string (5, 7, 8), twice. Fingers 1, 2 and 4, then 1, 3 and 4.
Start on a downstroke. The B string ends on a downstroke and the top string starts on an upstroke, so the pick travels around the outside of the pair at each change.
strings.exercise.three-per-string.six-note-up.co: Compare this with the descending take. A big difference is worth a note in your practice.
Now both kinds of crossing appear in one line, one straight after the other.
A up to B and back on the bottom three strings. First, third and little fingers on the low two strings. On the D string the little finger stretches a fret further, to fret 9.
When it is even both ways, the whole neck is the same idea with more strings.
At this speed a real rig's input delay can push notes out of their matching window, which reads as late or missed. Evenness is the number to trust here, and only once the delay is calibrated.
strings.exercise.three-per-string.six-strings.pu: The whole shape up and down in triplets, a small hand shift included where the top strings move up a fret.
strings.exercise.three-per-string.six-strings.ho: The hand moves up one fret when you reach the B string. Do it during the string change, not after it.
strings.exercise.three-per-string.six-strings.co: Long lines are where time drifts. Evenness across the whole take is the number.
strings.step.speed-bursts.title: Speed bursts
strings.step.speed-bursts.goal: Play short runs above your clean tempo, and land on time, without tensing up for the whole bar.
strings.step.speed-bursts.why: You can't practise speed by doing everything slowly and you can't do it by flailing. A burst is the honest middle: one beat of real speed, then a rest long enough that the hand lets go. Most players find a burst is several rungs above what they can sustain, and that tells them the wall is stamina or tension rather than how fast the fingers can go.
strings.step.speed-bursts.howTo.0: Rest between bursts. The rest is half the Exercise: let the hand go soft before the next one.
strings.step.speed-bursts.howTo.1: Aim at the landing note, not at the run. If you land on time, the run was fine.
strings.step.speed-bursts.howTo.2: Stay above your comfortable tempo here, and use the app's ramp to find where bursts stop being clean.
strings.step.speed-bursts.payoff: You will hear yourself play a short run far faster than you thought you could, and it will be clean.
strings.exercise.speed-bursts.one-beat.title: One beat on, one beat off
strings.exercise.speed-bursts.one-beat.purpose: The shortest honest burst: four notes and a landing, twice a bar.
strings.exercise.speed-bursts.one-beat.howTo.0: Four sixteenths up one string from fret 5, one finger per fret, then a quarter note on the third finger at fret 7. Twice a bar.
strings.exercise.speed-bursts.one-beat.howTo.1: Everything relaxes during the quarter note: let the hand go soft before the next burst. Start above the tempo you can hold for a whole bar.
strings.exercise.speed-bursts.one-beat.coachLine: Landing on time counts more than the run. Timing and missed notes are what I have here.
strings.exercise.speed-bursts.one-beat.detection: At this speed a real rig's input delay can push notes out of their matching window, which reads as late or missed. Evenness is the number to trust here, and only once the delay is calibrated.
strings.exercise.speed-bursts.one-beat.selfCheck: Did the last note land with the click, and did the hand let go in the rest?
strings.exercise.speed-bursts.two-beats.title: Two beats on, two off
strings.exercise.speed-bursts.two-beats.purpose: Twice the length with the same rest, so you find out how much of the speed survives eight notes.
strings.exercise.speed-bursts.two-beats.howTo.0: Eight sixteenths, up the four fingers from fret 5 and back, then a half note on fret 7.
strings.exercise.speed-bursts.two-beats.howTo.1: The halfway point of the run, where it turns round on the little finger, is where the time usually moves. Aim at the half note and let the run carry you there.
strings.exercise.speed-bursts.two-beats.coachLin: If one beat was clean and two is not, that is a stamina question and not a speed one.
strings.exercise.speed-bursts.two-beats.detectio: At this speed a real rig's input delay can push notes out of their matching window, which reads as late or missed. Evenness is the number to trust here, and only once the delay is calibrated.
strings.exercise.speed-bursts.expanding.title: Expanding bursts
strings.exercise.speed-bursts.expanding.purpose: One beat, then two, three and four beats on, the classic way of walking a burst into a line.
strings.exercise.speed-bursts.expanding.howTo.0: The bar tells you how long to keep going. Bar 4 has no rest, so the hand has to stay loose while moving.
strings.exercise.speed-bursts.expanding.coachLin: Most people slip somewhere in the third bar. It helps to know which one is yours.
strings.exercise.speed-bursts.expanding.detectio: At this speed a real rig's input delay can push notes out of their matching window, which reads as late or missed. Evenness is the number to trust here, and only once the delay is calibrated.
strings.exercise.speed-bursts.six-note-burst.tit: The six-note burst, into a landing
strings.exercise.speed-bursts.six-note-burst.pur: Your descending lick at sextuplet speed, then a walk down to A: this is how a fast run actually gets used in a solo.
strings.exercise.speed-bursts.six-note-burst.how: One beat of sextuplets from the top string, then D, C and A as quarter notes. Land exactly on beat 2.
strings.exercise.speed-bursts.six-note-burst.coa: Fast notes on a real rig are the hardest to time, so trust the landing and your own ear as much as the numbers.
strings.exercise.speed-bursts.six-note-burst.det: At this speed a real rig's input delay can push notes out of their matching window, which reads as late or missed. Evenness is the number to trust here, and only once the delay is calibrated.
strings.exercise.speed-bursts.six-note-burst.sel: On a recording, can you still hear all six notes as six?
strings.step.cross-string-runs.title: Cross-string runs
strings.step.cross-string-runs.goal: Keep alternate strokes going over string skips and long lines across all six strings.
strings.step.cross-string-runs.why: So far crossings have been a neighbour at a time. Real lines jump a string and cover the whole neck, and they make you aim. This is the Step where the pick stops following your fingers and starts knowing where it is going.
strings.step.cross-string-runs.howTo.0: On a skip, let the pick travel in a small arc over the string in between. Do not lift the whole forearm.
strings.step.cross-string-runs.howTo.1: Mute the strings you are not using with the side of the picking hand and with spare fretting fingers. Noise appears on crossings before it appears anywhere else.
strings.step.cross-string-runs.howTo.2: Read long lines in groups, not note by note.
strings.step.cross-string-runs.payoff: A climbing octave line, a chromatic crawl across all six strings, and an arpeggio line that sounds like a progression on its own.
strings.exercise.cross-string-runs.octaves.title: Octaves across a skipped string
strings.exercise.cross-string-runs.octaves.purpo: Every note is a string skip and the same two fingers do all the fretting, so the aim is all that is left to practise.
strings.exercise.cross-string-runs.octaves.howTo: First finger on the A string, third on the G string. Down on the A string, up on the G string, and a small shift between pairs. All of these are outside crossings.
strings.exercise.cross-string-runs.octaves.coach: If notes go missing here it is usually the skip or the shift. Slow down until neither is a surprise.
strings.exercise.cross-string-runs.spider.title: The chromatic crawl
strings.exercise.cross-string-runs.spider.purpos: One finger per fret on all six strings, up and back. It is not music, and it is the fastest way to find which crossing or finger is weak.
Up with 1-2-3-4 on each string and back with 4-3-2-1. Keep each finger down until the next string needs it.
strings.exercise.cross-string-runs.spider.coachL: This is a diagnostic, so play it slowly enough to hear the weakest change.
strings.exercise.cross-string-runs.scale-in-four: A long scale line in groups of four, up and back on three strings: this is what most fast lines are made of.
Each group starts one scale note higher. Stay with the beat: the first note of each group lands on it.
The turn around at the top is the place to listen to.
strings.exercise.cross-string-runs.picked-arpegg: Picked arpeggios: Am, F, C, G
Four strings, strict alternate strokes, and a chord progression you can hear in the single notes. The hand barely moves and it sounds like a whole band.
Each bar is one chord, up and down twice. Am to F moves one note. Stay in fifth position.
These are picked, not swept: every stroke alternates even though the notes run across strings.
I'll check the notes against the chords after the take. Whether it rings like a chord or sounds separated is yours to judge.
strings.step.up-to-tempo.title: Up to tempo
strings.step.up-to-tempo.goal: Take the lick, the three-string scale and the six-note pattern you already know up to the tempo real lines are played at.
strings.step.up-to-tempo.why: Everything so far was passed at a moderate tempo, where a slightly big stroke still works. Twenty clicks higher it doesn't: the motion has to get smaller, not faster, and the crossings you could think about now have to happen by themselves. These are figures you know, so the only new thing is the speed.
strings.step.up-to-tempo.howTo.0: Start two rungs below the tempo you passed the figure at, and listen for the first rung where it stops sounding easy. That rung is today's work; stay on it.
strings.step.up-to-tempo.howTo.1: Make the stroke smaller as the tempo rises. If the forearm tightens, drop a rung and find the small stroke again.
strings.step.up-to-tempo.howTo.2: Use the bursts from the Step before: play one beat at the new tempo and stop, then two beats, before you try the loop.
strings.step.up-to-tempo.payoff: The A minor lick at a tempo that sounds fast, and a two-octave scale run that holds together.
strings.exercise.up-to-tempo.licks-at-tempo.purp: The all-outside lick for a bar, then its mirror with every crossing inside, for a bar. Side by side at speed, the weaker crossing has nowhere to hide.
strings.exercise.up-to-tempo.licks-at-tempo.howT: Sixteenths. Bar 1 is the outside lick twice, starting on the D string. Bar 2 stays on the G and B strings, starting on a downstroke on the G string, and every crossing in it is inside.
If one bar is clean and the other is not, practise the other alone for a minute and come back.
strings.exercise.up-to-tempo.licks-at-tempo.coac: I'll say how even each bar was and check the notes after the take. At this speed evenness is the number to trust.
strings.exercise.up-to-tempo.licks-at-tempo.dete: At this speed a real rig's input delay can push notes out of their matching window, which reads as late or missed. Evenness is the number to trust here, and only once the delay is calibrated.
strings.exercise.up-to-tempo.three-strings-at-te: The three-notes-per-string run up and back, from three different starting strings, at a tempo where the stretch and the crossings have to be automatic.
Sixteenths, sixteen notes, strictly down-up. The crossings alternate outside and inside going up.
Keep the fingers close to the strings. At this tempo a finger that lifts high arrives late.
I'll say how even it was and check the notes after the take.
At this speed a real rig's input delay can push notes out of their matching window, which reads as late or missed. Evenness is the number to trust here, and only once the delay is calibrated.
strings.exercise.up-to-tempo.sextuplet-loop.titl: The six-note lick, six to a click
strings.exercise.up-to-tempo.sextuplet-loop.purp: C, B, A, G, F, E on the top two strings as sextuplets, round and round. The burst from the Step before, now without the rest after it.
strings.exercise.up-to-tempo.sextuplet-loop.howT: Six notes to the click, starting on a downstroke; the pattern is even, so every repeat starts down too.
Lean on the first note of each beat a little. Without it six fast notes turn into a blur with no beat in it.
strings.exercise.up-to-tempo.sextuplet-loop.coac: Fast notes are the hardest for me to place, so read the evenness as provisional and trust a recording as well.
strings.exercise.up-to-tempo.sextuplet-loop.dete: At this speed a real rig's input delay can push notes out of their matching window, which reads as late or missed. Evenness is the number to trust here, and only once the delay is calibrated.
strings.exercise.up-to-tempo.sextuplet-loop.self: On a recording, can you still hear all six notes as six?
strings.exercise.up-to-tempo.two-octave-run.titl: Two and a half octaves in sixteenths
strings.exercise.up-to-tempo.two-octave-run.purp: All six strings of A minor, three notes per string, up and back in sixteenths, with a held note to finish. The long run from the Intermediate Level, a third faster.
strings.exercise.up-to-tempo.two-octave-run.howT: The hand moves up one fret at the B string and again at the top string, and back on the way down. Move during the string change.
Read it in strings, not in notes: three, three, three. The beat falls on a different finger each time, so keep the click in your ear.
strings.exercise.up-to-tempo.two-octave-run.coac: This is the Step's test piece. I'll say how even it was and check the notes after the take.
strings.exercise.up-to-tempo.two-octave-run.dete: At this speed a real rig's input delay can push notes out of their matching window, which reads as late or missed. Evenness is the number to trust here, and only once the delay is calibrated.
strings.step.stamina-minute.title: The stamina minute
strings.step.stamina-minute.goal: Hold an even line for sixty seconds at a tempo you could play for ten.
strings.step.stamina-minute.why: Speed that lasts four bars is a party trick. Holding a tempo for a minute is what shows you are not playing on tension, because tension is what runs out. It also gives you honest information: the last ten seconds show the real state of your technique.
strings.step.stamina-minute.howTo.0: Choose a rung about 20% below your clean tempo. It should feel slow for the first ten seconds.
strings.step.stamina-minute.howTo.1: Breathe. If the shoulder comes up, drop it during a bar line without stopping.
strings.step.stamina-minute.howTo.2: Stop at any pain in the hand, wrist or forearm. A tired forearm is one thing and pain is another; pain ends the set.
strings.step.stamina-minute.payoff: A full minute of sixteenths that sounds the same at the end as at the start.
strings.exercise.stamina-minute.chromatic-minute: Stamina without any other question: the four-finger walk for a whole minute.
The sixteenth-note walk, sixty seconds, no stops. If the time slips late in the take, the rung was too high.
If I stop catching notes on a long take, trust that report over your doubts about your hands. Long unbroken playing is something the listening has not been proven on.

Long unbroken playing, especially high-gain, can drown out where each note starts, so the app may stop hearing you. Unproven either way; if the app says it did not catch enough, believe that before you doubt your hands.
strings.exercise.stamina-minute.box-minute.title: One minute, the box
strings.exercise.stamina-minute.box-minute.purpo: The same minute with crossings in it, which is where stamina really gets used.
strings.exercise.stamina-minute.box-minute.howTo: Box 1 of A minor pentatonic at fret 5, all six strings up and back, in triplets, three to the click, for one minute without stopping.
Keep the crossings small: they grow as you tire. If the pick starts catching on the way across, the rung was too high.
strings.exercise.stamina-minute.box-minute.coach: Compare the first and last quarter of the take. A drop there is the point of doing this.
strings.exercise.stamina-minute.box-minute.detec: Long unbroken playing, especially high-gain, can drown out where each note starts, so the app may stop hearing you. Unproven either way; if the app says it did not catch enough, believe that before you doubt your hands.
strings.exercise.stamina-minute.scale-minute.pur: The hardest of the three: three strings of A minor up and back, sixteenths, with both crossing types.
strings.exercise.stamina-minute.scale-minute.how: Sixty seconds. If this one falls apart well before the others did, go back to crossings for a few days, as it is not an endurance problem.
strings.exercise.stamina-minute.scale-minute.coa: When the box and this one hold up side by side, you are ready for the band.
strings.exercise.stamina-minute.scale-minute.det: Long unbroken playing, especially high-gain, can drown out where each note starts, so the app may stop hearing you. Unproven either way; if the app says it did not catch enough, believe that before you doubt your hands.
strings.step.over-the-band.title: A clean run over the band
strings.step.over-the-band.goal: Play an eight-bar line over Am, F, C, G with a real band behind you, and stay even when the click is no longer the only thing in your ears.
strings.step.over-the-band.why: A click forgives nothing and a band hides everything, which is why this is a separate skill. The drums give you a pulse with a feel to it, the bass tells you where the changes are, and your line has to fit between them. This is the reason you did all of the rest.
strings.step.over-the-band.howTo.0: Every written line lands on a tone of the chord on each bar line. Play it dry first and hear that happen.
strings.step.over-the-band.howTo.1: Listen to the snare, not to your own fingers. If you get lost, catch the next bar line and carry on.
strings.step.over-the-band.howTo.2: Use direct input or headphones for a graded take: the band reaching a microphone is something the app has not been tested against.
strings.step.over-the-band.payoff: You play a solo-length line over a band and it sounds like you meant it.
strings.exercise.over-the-band.etude-eighths.pur: A composed line at a rate you can certainly play, so the band is the only new thing.
strings.exercise.over-the-band.etude-eighths.how: Eighth notes for eight bars: Am, F, C, G, twice round, all in fifth position on the top four strings.
Every bar starts on a note of its chord, so hear the bar lines land. Bar 8 climbs back toward the A where the line starts again.
strings.exercise.over-the-band.etude-eighths.coa: Band on, and all I need is that you stay with it. I'll report the notes after the take.
strings.exercise.over-the-band.etude-eighths.det: With a microphone and speakers the band reaches the same input as you. Direct input or headphones are the honest way to grade this; without them it is untested.
strings.exercise.over-the-band.etude-mixed.title: Four bars, eighths into sixteenths
strings.exercise.over-the-band.etude-mixed.purpo: A fill at the end of every bar. Changing gear in time with a band is what makes a line sound like a player, not like a pattern.
strings.exercise.over-the-band.etude-mixed.howTo: Let the eighths sit back, and let the sixteenths lead into the next bar line, without speeding up.
strings.exercise.over-the-band.etude-mixed.coach: The fills are what tend to rush. Listening back to one take with the band is often enough to hear it.
strings.exercise.over-the-band.etude-mixed.detec: With a microphone and speakers the band reaches the same input as you. Direct input or headphones are the honest way to grade this; without them it is untested.
At this speed a real rig's input delay can push notes out of their matching window, which reads as late or missed. Evenness is the number to trust here, and only once the delay is calibrated.
The whole Path in four bars: the outside lick, a picked arpeggio, a C arpeggio that reaches up, and a scale run home.
The groove stays on eighths and you sit on twice its rate. Each bar is one of the ideas you have already practised, so it is mostly a matter of joining them.
This is the graded line. Fast notes on a real rig are the hardest for me to place, so I'd trust the evenness and your ear together.
With a microphone and speakers the band reaches the same input as you. Direct input or headphones are the honest way to grade this; without them it is untested.
At this speed a real rig's input delay can push notes out of their matching window, which reads as late or missed. Evenness is the number to trust here, and only once the delay is calibrated.
strings.exercise.over-the-band.full-run.title: The whole run, your take
strings.exercise.over-the-band.full-run.purpose: The eighths, then the sixteenths, as one take. Record it and listen back: this one is for you, and no number decides it.
strings.exercise.over-the-band.full-run.howTo.0: Eight bars of the eighth-note line, then four of the sixteenth line, at whatever rung you can play both. Keep the take if you like it.
strings.exercise.over-the-band.full-run.coachLin: No score on this one. Listen back, and if you would play it for someone, the Path is done.
strings.exercise.over-the-band.full-run.detectio: With a microphone and speakers the band reaches the same input as you. Direct input or headphones are the honest way to grade this; without them it is untested.
strings.exercise.over-the-band.full-run.selfChec: Did every bar line land with the band?
Do the sixteenths sound as relaxed as the eighths?
Would you be happy for another guitarist to hear this take?
strings.level.beginner.title: Beginner: one string, even
strings.level.beginner.summary: Eighths, sixteenths and accents on a single string, so that time and control come before crossing strings.
strings.level.beginner.startHereIf.0: You can fret single notes cleanly and you hold a pick.
strings.level.beginner.startHereIf.1: You can play eighth notes with a click at 80 BPM, but sixteenths come out uneven.
strings.level.beginner.startHereIf.2: An accent on an upstroke feels foreign, or you've never tried one.
strings.exercise.warmup-beginner.one-string-clim: Eighths up one string in a minor key, climbing a scale step each bar. A different string and key each time, so there's a tune to follow and a reason to move.
Start well under your clean tempo. Follow the tune and let the hand travel with it.
This is a warm-up. It tells you how it went, and it decides nothing.
strings.level.intermediate.title: Intermediate: across the strings
strings.level.intermediate.summary: Both kinds of crossing, then the two shapes that use them most: the pentatonic box and three notes per string.
strings.level.intermediate.startHereIf.0: You can hold even sixteenths on one string at about 85 BPM.
strings.level.intermediate.startHereIf.1: You can put an accent on any sixteenth, including on an upstroke, without the time moving.
strings.level.intermediate.startHereIf.2: Your line falls apart when it changes string.
A short pentatonic lick moved through i, iv and v of a minor key, in a different key and with a different lick each time.
Start well under your clean tempo. The hand moves at the bar line, and the strokes don't change.
This is a warm-up. It tells you how it went, and it decides nothing.
strings.level.advanced.title: Advanced: speed, length and a band
strings.level.advanced.summary: Bursts above your clean tempo, string skips and long lines, the figures you know taken up to tempo, a full minute without letting up, then a composed run over a band.
strings.level.advanced.startHereIf.0: You can run A minor three notes per string, across three strings, even at sixteenths 80 BPM.
strings.level.advanced.startHereIf.1: You can name which crossing is your weaker one.
strings.level.advanced.startHereIf.2: Clean is fine at a moderate tempo and you've hit a speed wall, or you've never played with a band.
strings.exercise.warmup-advanced.scale-round.pur: Three strings of a minor scale, up and back from two positions on the neck, starting from a different root each time.
strings.exercise.warmup-advanced.scale-round.how: Start well under your clean tempo. Change position at the bar line. Keep the shift as small as you can.
strings.exercise.warmup-advanced.scale-round.coa: This is a warm-up. It tells you how it went, and it decides nothing.
